title: The Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark: Do Language Models Know the Foundations of Early-Grade Literacy?
abstract: arXiv:2611.34823v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many languages of instruction in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are poorly represented in the data used to train language models. Before these models can support early-grade literacy in such languages, we need to know whether they hold the linguistic knowledge of each language that literacy teaching relies on. To test this, we present the Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark and the reproducible, largely automated pipeline that turns curriculum documents, teacher guides and pupil books into a vetted question set organised on a fixed grid of nine linguistic domains and seven grade levels. The pipeline combines LLM-driven source survey, feature consolidation, item generation and quality control with an item-selection step inspired by item response theory and a final expert review. translated_title: 语言知识基准：语言模型是否掌握早期年级读写能力的根基？
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.34823v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：在低收入和中等收入国家（LMICs），许多教学语言在用于训练语言模型的数据中代表性不足。在这些模型能够支持此类语言的早期年级读写教育之前，我们需要了解它们是否掌握读写教学所依赖的每种语言的语言学知识。为了检验这一点，我们提出了语言知识基准以及一个可复现、大部分自动化的流程，该流程将课程文件、教师指南和学生用书转化为经过审核的题目集，题目按固定的网格组织，涵盖九个语言学领域和七个年级。该流程结合了LLM驱动的源文献调查、特征整合、题目生成和质量控制，并辅以受项目反应理论启发的题目选择步骤和最终的专家评审。我们为基斯瓦希里语（肯尼亚；135道题）和英语（英国；137道题）实例化了该流程，并分别评估了121个和119个模型。前沿模型表……
tldr: 该论文提出了语言知识基准及一套可复现的自动化流程，将课程文件转化为涵盖九个语言学领域和七个年级的审核题目集，用于检验语言模型是否具备支持低收入和中等收入国家早期读写教学所需的语言学知识，并以基斯瓦希里语和英语为实例评估了两百多个模型。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces the Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark, a reproducible, largely automated pipeline that converts curriculum documents into vetted question sets across nine linguistic domains and seven grade levels to test whether language models possess the linguistic knowledge required for early-grade literacy instruction, instantiated for Kiswahili and English with over 240 models evaluated.
